text: If you want that deep an influence — if you just want to stay at an HCI paper, then you can publish the paper and be done. [Amber: that's a very good critique; what you just said could deeply wound this community — you people only do it to publish a paper; if there were no paper to publish you wouldn't even make the thing. But this costs money, right? It's a resource issue.] It costs effort — you have to ally with and use every resource around you.
gist: Critique of paper-driven incentives; real influence requires effort and mobilising all available resources.
zh: 那如果你想影响那么深远的话，如果你想stay at HCI paper，那就不需要发完paper完事儿。[A: 我觉得这是很好的critique。你刚才说的一句话非常好，我觉得可以深深地刺伤这个社区，就是你们这些人就是为了发paper，不然不发paper，你们写都不会写。但这里面就要花钱，对吧？就是资源的问题。一定要花钱。] 哦，是花心思。要去联合，去把你身边所有能用的resource都用上。
source: Cross-project coauthor dialogue, 1 Aug 2026; ASR transcript translated 2026-08-29; audio verification pending

text: [Amber: what resources did you use?] Various endangered-species public accounts, all that kind of account. [Amber: how did you find the lawsuit?] A friend of mine was working on nine cases, mainly civil ones; I said I'm following animal issues lately, could you find me some animal-related cases? And he found this one.
gist: Elephant campaign resources: endangered-species social accounts and a lawyer friend who surfaced the animal-welfare case.
zh: [A: 当时用了什么？] 各种濒危物种。那些公众账号，就是各种这类的账号。[A: 你当时是怎么发现这个诉讼案的？] 我个朋友他在做九个案子，但是他做的主要是民事的，然后我就说你能不能我最近在关注对于动物的，能不能帮我找一些跟动物的案子？然后他找到了这个。
source: Cross-project coauthor dialogue, 1 Aug 2026; ASR transcript translated 2026-08-29; audio verification pending

text: So the process was mainly about connecting forces you could mobilise — it's a bit like activism. [Jiabao: it is activism.] So the responsibility goes beyond that of a traditional maker. [Jiabao: those projects were made with the same group of Chinese friends who all do socially engaged art.]
gist: Elephant campaign was activism done with socially-engaged-art collaborators; responsibility extends beyond making.
zh: 这过程中其实主要更多是联系能够发动的力量，对吧？所以这个有点像activism。[J: 这个是activism。] 所以说他有时候责任已经beyond一个传统的负责人了。[J: 我那几个项目都是跟同一批中国的朋友做的，他们全都是艺术介入社会这一类的。]
source: Cross-project coauthor dialogue, 1 Aug 2026; ASR transcript translated 2026-08-29; audio verification pending

text: Socially engaged art is similar to the logic of more-than-human intervening in society: how to intervene, how to turn it into civic infrastructure — I call it becoming civic infrastructure. [Jiabao: he mapped out a whole atlas of art infrastructure; we could map that onto this.] The problems my paper addresses are the ones artists have always had to solve — feminist artists did the same, indigenous-culture artists did the same: how to make art, then how to spread it and be remembered. It's the same problem.
gist: MtH reach/decay problems are not new; socially engaged, feminist and indigenous art already faced them — tactics importable.
zh: 艺术介入社会，其实这个也是有点像是把more-than-human介入社会的逻辑，就是你怎么样去介入社会，怎么样把它变成一个civic infrastructure，我把它叫做成为公民的基础设施。[J: 其实他艺术基础设施，他当时铺了一堆的图谱，有可能可以把那个图谱映射到这上面看。] 对，其实我这篇文章要解决的问题，都是艺术家本身要解决的问题。当年做feminist的artist也做过同样的事情，然后那些做indigenous culture人也做过这样的事情，这就是如何艺术好做，做完以后怎么传播，怎么让别人记住你。它解决的是同样的问题。
source: Cross-project coauthor dialogue, 1 Aug 2026; ASR transcript translated 2026-08-29; audio verification pending

text: There are other methods; we could brainstorm what can strengthen propagation. Like putting it [Mouse Coach] on the App Store so many people can download it — that's one. But then how do you promote it there?
gist: App Store distribution as a propagation channel, with the open problem of promotion.
zh: 还有其他的办法，比如说，我们现在就可以brainstorm，都有什么可以什么办法可以对增强传播？像我们把那个登到了App Store上面，很多人可以下载，这也可以。但又需要怎么在上面推广？
source: Cross-project coauthor dialogue, 1 Aug 2026; ASR transcript translated 2026-08-29; audio verification pending

text: What did Eliasson's Ice Watch rely on? On the Paris climate summit's own newsworthiness. [Jiabao: plus he's a very famous artist himself.] That I can't count — because we want to distil the technique as the final contribution. [Jiabao: so, target something big that already has many eyeballs; that's how you make bread.]
gist: Ice Watch hitchhiked on the Paris climate summit's attention; fame is excluded from distillable tactics.
zh: 那当时其实我想，那个Eliasson做那个Ice Watch，它靠的是什么？它靠的是巴黎气候大会这个本身的噱头。[J: 然后加上他自己也是个很有名的artist。] 这个我就不能算。从手法上，就是我说为什么不能算，就是因为我们想把最后的方法technique distill出来，蒸馏出来，变成最后的contribution。[J: 就target something big，就有很多人眼球的，这样能make bread。]
source: Cross-project coauthor dialogue, 1 Aug 2026; ASR transcript translated 2026-08-29; audio verification pending

text: Was your use of the court similar — does a court, like the Paris climate summit, naturally carry topicality? [Jiabao: yes, but it's also different, because we genuinely wanted to fight for nature — we hoped China could pass such a law.]
gist: Court as attention-bearing venue, but Jiabao stresses the litigation was sincere advocacy, not only a publicity device.
zh: 其实当时你做那个法庭是不是也是类似，法院是不是类似跟巴黎气候大会那个一样，天然具有一定的话题性？[J: 对。但是又不太一样，因为那个是我们真的想fight for nature的，就希望中国能有这样一条法律来通过。]
source: Cross-project coauthor dialogue, 1 Aug 2026; ASR transcript translated 2026-08-29; audio verification pending

gist: Court as attention-bearing venue, but Jiabao stresses the litigation was sincere advocacy, not only a publicity device.
zh: 其实当时你做那个法庭是不是也是类似，法院是不是类似跟巴黎气候大会那个一样，天然具有一定的话题性？[J: 对。但是又不太一样，因为那个是我们真的想fight for nature的，就希望中国能有这样一条法律来通过。]
source: Cross-project coauthor dialogue, 1 Aug 2026; ASR transcript translated 2026-08-29; audio verification pending

text: For instance, make the product something you can integrate into daily life. The Mouse Coach project [ASR 'TDHD'] could go much deeper — even become a health startup: people buy a smart running wheel and subscribe to my mouse, everybody runs toward [it]; then the mouse's impact could live in everyone's home, in everyone's body. [Amber: that belongs to the later part — what endures after noticing.]
gist: Productisation (smart running wheel health startup) as a route for Mouse Coach's noticing to endure in daily life.
zh: 比如说，把把这种product做成到something you can integrate into daily life. 我TDHD可能那个那个项目还有很很多可以深的接着做，甚至可以把它变成一个health startup，就真真的，大家可以买一个smart running wheel，然后subscribe to my mouse，everybody run towards，如果那样的话，就是真的能，就是这个mouse的impact能住到每个人的家里，住到每个人的身。[A: 这个就属于我觉得后面那部分，就是它能够what endures，after noticing。]
source: Cross-project coauthor dialogue, 1 Aug 2026; ASR transcript translated 2026-08-29; audio verification pending

text: We made the app and exhibited it everywhere, and during exhibitions organised running events: people come run together while discussing animal welfare. Runners wear a bib that says 'Mouse Coach running', so passers-by ask 'what is that?', and through the asking more people get to know about it.
gist: Mouse Coach's public running events with bibs recruited passers-by through curiosity.
zh: 做了app到处展，然后展的期间会organize running event，然后run的时候就就大家过来一起run，一边讨论animal welfare。然后因为run的时候会戴那个胸牌儿，然后上面写mouse coach running，然后很多人经过what is that，然后就会问问的时候大家就是会更更增加更多人的人知道。
source: Cross-project coauthor dialogue, 1 Aug 2026; ASR transcript translated 2026-08-29; audio verification pending

text: That part is the same as EchoVision: you need physical branding — your form factor or whatever — to invite others' curiosity. [Jiabao: right, you bring it to the public space and people come over.] I think 'in the wild' is very important — public space.
gist: Physical branding/form in public space ('in the wild') as a shared reach tactic of Mouse Coach and EchoVision.
zh: 那这个部分是跟EchoVision一样的，就是需要有physical的branding。要么是你的造型或什么样，就是要invite别人的好奇心。[J: 对，you bring it to the public space，然后别人过来。] 我觉得in the wild非常重要，就是public space。
source: Cross-project coauthor dialogue, 1 Aug 2026; ASR transcript translated 2026-08-29; audio verification pending

text: That part is the same as EchoVision: you need physical branding — your form factor or whatever — to invite others' curiosity. [Jiabao: right, you bring it to the public space and people come over.] I think 'in the wild' is very important — public space.

source: Cross-project coauthor dialogue, 1 Aug 2026; ASR transcript translated 2026-08-29; audio verification pending

text: In the end it's about how art breaks out of its circle — the art world is too small. [Amber: most break-outs rely on exhibitions, on the curator system, on curation.]
gist: 'Breaking out' (出圈) of the small art circle; curatorial system is the default channel.
zh: 对，就是艺，回到底就是艺术怎么出圈嘛？艺术圈太小了，然后出圈的方式。[A: 大部分出圈是靠展览，就是靠那个curator system，就是靠creation。]
source: Cross-project coauthor dialogue, 1 Aug 2026; ASR transcript translated 2026-08-29; audio verification pending

text: Where you differ is that you often show in civic infrastructure — the running is in civic infrastructure, and our EchoVision under the bridge in a public park is civic infrastructure too — so it goes beyond traditional curation in art venues. [Jiabao: the elephant too, spread online in influencer style.] So these three works differ essentially in propagation path; but Mouse Coach is still mostly gallery-based, adding some civic participation outside the gallery — its base is the gallery system.
gist: Comparative propagation paths: EchoVision and Mouse Coach in civic infrastructure atop a gallery base; elephant via online virality.
zh: 所以说你这边有difference地方是在于你经常是放在公民的基础设施中展示，比如说你说跑步是在公民基础设施中，包括我们的EchoVision也是在桥下，也是public park，是一个公民基础设施，所以它beyond了传统的curation在艺术的场域中进行展示。[J: 大象也是，网上传播，以网红的方式。] 所以说这三件作品其实本质上是它的传播路径，但是Mouse Coach大部分也是基于画廊传播，在画廊之外采用一些公民的参与，它的基础点还是基于画廊的系统。
source: Cross-project coauthor dialogue, 1 Aug 2026; ASR transcript translated 2026-08-29; audio verification pending

text: The socially engaged artists I collaborate with are not confined to galleries; they look down on galleries and the curatorial system because what they do can't happen in that circle. For instance swapping water — taking water from a polluted area and swapping it with Nongfu Spring, then opening a pop-up store in Beijing so people could buy the polluted water. Or turning a polluted river ditch into 'hotpot fish', dumping big fish in and ladling them out like hotpot, because the river was polluted completely red.
gist: Socially engaged art examples (polluted-water pop-up store, hotpot fish) show mature outside-gallery intervention tactics.
zh: 跟我一起合作的这批做艺术介入社会的人，他们不局限于画廊，他们特别瞧不上画廊和你的自由系统，因为他们觉得他们所做的事就没办法在这个circle里面进行。比如说给小豪说换水呀，把一个水污染的区域，然后跟农夫山泉换，然后在北京做一个pop up store，让大家来买这种污染的水。还有把一个污染的河沟做成火锅鱼，然后搞了一大堆的大鱼放进去，然后拿大勺捞火锅。因为那个河污染的全红色了。
source: Cross-project coauthor dialogue, 1 Aug 2026; ASR transcript translated 2026-08-29; audio verification pending

text: But I feel most more-than-human work is done quietly on one's own, playing with plants alone. What I'm asking is: is that intentional, or do people simply lack awareness of tactics, or lack the tactics? The tactics could be borrowed wholesale from socially engaged art. Or do these more-than-human designers only do it to finish a paper?
gist: Open question whether MtH designers' inwardness is intentional, a lack of tactical awareness, or paper-driven.
zh: 但我就觉得more-than-human第三大分都是暗搓搓在做，就自己一个人跟植物在玩。我今天这样讨论就是，它是intentionally这么做，还是大家根本没有这个tactic这个意识，还是说没有这个tactic？我觉得这个tactic完全可以像艺术界那些介入社会介入艺术去借鉴。只是说这些more than human的designer他完全就是为了完成paper才做的呢，还是什么？
source: Cross-project coauthor dialogue, 1 Aug 2026; ASR transcript translated 2026-08-29; audio verification pending

text: Your ice piece — does that count as eco art? [Jiabao: I can't call it design. There's no design in it. What can be called design has a user; there's no user in that. You design for someone.]
gist: Jiabao's criterion: design requires a user; her ice printing is art, not design.
zh: 你你做的冰色Eco Art。那个算不算Eco Art呢？[J: 呃，design。我不能称之为design。没有design在里面。就我感觉能称之为design的，它就是有有一个user，我这里面都没有user。你design for someone。]
source: Cross-project coauthor dialogue, 1 Aug 2026; ASR transcript translated 2026-08-29; audio verification pending

text: Does your definition of more-than-human include AI? [Jiabao: yes, both.] Does it include ghosts? [Jiabao: probably, but I haven't made any yet.] People always say they do more-than-human; I test them with these three questions. [Jiabao: I don't like the term, because it includes so much that it includes nothing. But there's no single word that covers what we want to describe — animals, plants, and, say, glaciers.]
gist: Definitional instability of 'more-than-human' (AI? ghosts? gods?); Jiabao dislikes the term's emptiness.
zh: 在你的more-than-human的定义中存不存在AI？[J: 存在，两个都存在。] 你的more-than-human存不存在鬼？[J: 应该存在吧，但我还没做过这些。] 经常大家说我们都是做more-than-human的，我一般就用这三个问题测试。[J: 我不喜欢这个词，因为它包含了太多，以至于不包含任何东西。那就是没有一个词可以去去包含我们想形容的，就是有animal，plant，还有，比如说glacier。]
source: Cross-project coauthor dialogue, 1 Aug 2026; ASR transcript translated 2026-08-29; audio verification pending

text: Animism — 'all things have spirit'. I'd like to hear your view on animism, like Japanese Shinto. Animism originally wouldn't include AI, but now people call it cyber animism — Joscha Bach proposed cyber animism.
gist: Animism / cyber-animism (Bach) as an alternative framing to MtH design.
zh: 万物有灵啊，就是animism。所以说，我我也想听一下你对animism的看法。就是日本的这个神道教。在animism里面应该不存在AI的吧？当年，现在就管人家叫cyber animism。这个Joscha Bach，他提出了这个就是cyber animism。
source: Cross-project coauthor dialogue, 1 Aug 2026; ASR transcript translated 2026-08-29; audio verification pending

text: I've been learning about Japanese culture. The yōkai ghosts are fascinating — really animism: a slipper worn for a thousand years gains a spirit. Chinese yaoguai are even grander and more imaginative. [Amber: does your more-than-human include yōkai?] It does, I think. I actually have an upcoming project related to yōkai.
gist: Yōkai/yaoguai as animist entities within Jiabao's MtH scope; a planned yōkai project.
zh: 在学习一些日本文化。有凯那些鬼魂里面很有意思，就是对，就真的是万物有灵。一个一个穿了一千年的拖鞋，然后里面可以，就其实跟中国的那些妖怪，就其实中国的妖怪比有凯更更大，更有想象力。[A: 在你more-than-human中，包不包含妖怪？] 包含，我觉得包含。我其实有下一个要跟妖怪做的有关的项目。
source: Cross-project coauthor dialogue, 1 Aug 2026; ASR transcript translated 2026-08-29; audio verification pending

text: How do you see Japanese animism versus current more-than-human theory — how does animism do noticing? [Jiabao: it's already a belief. Once it's a belief, it's everywhere.] Right, that's the highest state. My biggest heresy is: if you want to promote more-than-human design, you might as well promote animism, cyber animism.
gist: Belief (animism) as the asymptote of augmented noticing — noticing without artefacts.
zh: 你怎么看日式的万物有灵和现在的more-than-human理论？就是日本的万物有灵中，他怎么做noticing？[J: 这已经是一个belief了。对啊，一旦是你这个belief，你就到处都是了。] 对啊，所以这才是我觉得最高境界。其实说，我觉得我的最大谬论是说，如果要去宣传什么more-than-human design，你不如宣传animism，cyber animism。
source: Cross-project coauthor dialogue, 1 Aug 2026; ASR transcript translated 2026-08-29; audio verification pending

text: But wouldn't animism count as a faith — and once something is a faith, many people are not very open to it? [Amber: but more-than-human design is also a faith, in my view.] It's a methodology. [Amber: basically a faith: we believe we live in an interdependent world, and that through design interventions we need more people to realise that.] Right, basically the eco-simple [unclear] thing.
gist: Disagreement: Jiabao worries belief triggers resistance and calls MtH a methodology; Amber says MtH design is already functionally a belief.
zh: 但是会不会说就是？Animism相当是一种信仰，然后很多人觉得，哦，一旦是一个信仰，他就会not very open to it。[A: 那现在问题是，more than human design也是个信仰，在我看。] 是一个methodology。[A: 我觉得基本是信仰嘛，我的这边基本信仰是说，我们认为，我们生活在一个interdependence的一个世界。同时呢，我们需要通过design这种intervention，让更多的人意识到我们在一个interdependence世界。] 对对对，基本上就是那个echo，echo simple那个。
source: Cross-project coauthor dialogue, 1 Aug 2026; ASR transcript translated 2026-08-29; audio verification pending

text: It's a faith: we believe that if we make others aware, the problem is solved. [Jiabao: but this faith needs more missionaries so more people share it.] Missionaries of the design itself, or of interdependence itself? I think more-than-human design currently broadcasts entirely to other designers, not to the public. Broadcasting to the public means spreading it like animism. [Jiabao: right — an inner circle jerk.]
gist: MtH design evangelises other designers rather than the public ('inner circle jerk').
zh: 对，这是个信仰，就是我们相信，我们让别人意识到了，这个事情就能解决。[J: 但是这个信仰，我们需要更多的传道者去让大家，更多的人，去有同样的信仰。] 那这个传道者是说是传达这个design本身，还是你要传导这个interdependence本身，我觉得现在More-than-Human Design完全是在给其他的designer做传播，而不是在给公众做传播。我觉得给公众传播的本质就是你要像animism一样传播。[J: 对，Inner Circle Jerk。]
source: Cross-project coauthor dialogue, 1 Aug 2026; ASR transcript translated 2026-08-29; audio verification pending

text: [Amber: when you make work you usually use a lot of humour or exaggeration — the goal is to let more people know, right?] Yes. Because of climate fatigue people are closed to this topic; humour lets them open up, and once open they accept what you want to say. At this past exhibition many people told me 'you make people think and then laugh' — no: you make people laugh, and then you make people think. That's a very good state.
gist: Humour as an opener against climate fatigue: 'make people laugh, then make people think'.
zh: [A: 你在做作品的时候，一般会采用很多幽默的手段，或者说一些比较夸张的手段。他的目标其实是为了让更多人知道对吧？] 对，因为就是climate fatigue，大家对这个topic很close，然后用humor可以让大家open up，然后一旦open up，他就会能更接受你想说的东西。然后比如说我，这个过去这个展，他说有好多人跟我说，you make people think，and then you make people laugh。哦，no，you make people laugh，and then you make people think。就是一个很好的状态。
source: Cross-project coauthor dialogue, 1 Aug 2026; ASR transcript translated 2026-08-29; audio verification pending

text: But most more-than-human design — in that paper I just looked at — hardly any make people laugh. [Jiabao: right, and many are far-fetched: they claim doing this makes people feel that, but only the author feels it.]
gist: Few MtH works use humour; many claims about audience feeling are wishful and author-only.
zh: But大部分的more-than-human design，我刚看那篇paper嘛，没有几个是make people laugh。[J: 对，而且有很多就很牵强。就是说你这样做就能让人这么觉得，但是只有作者本身是这么觉得的。]
source: Cross-project coauthor dialogue, 1 Aug 2026; ASR transcript translated 2026-08-29; audio verification pending

text: There's something important here about what endures: through an intervention like laughter you produce neuroplastic change, and embodied methods work the same way. For example, echolocating is an embodied call; you perform some abnormal actions and those abnormal actions produce neuroplastic change — more effective than me telling you in words that bats echolocate.
gist: Embodiment (echolocating) and humour produce durable neuroplastic change where verbal telling does not.
zh: 所以我觉得这里面有很重要的东西，就我刚才说，what endures，就是你通过laugh这种intervention让大家产生一个neuroplasticity，就是神经可塑性的改变，包括你用具身性的方法也是一样的。比如说，echolocation是具身性的叫，然后你产生一些很不正常的行动，这些不正常的行动那里会产生神经可塑性的改变，比我跟你直接用语言说蝙蝠是echolocation的，来的更有效。
source: Cross-project coauthor dialogue, 1 Aug 2026; ASR transcript translated 2026-08-29; audio verification pending

text: That's what I call augmented noticing: I could tell you in words to notice the bat over there, but to give you a deeper memory I use embodiment, humour, all sorts — artistic means, really. [Jiabao: Mouse Coach too — you have to really run a lot before you understand they run that much every day.] And calling out also makes bystanders notice you — 'how odd, why are they shouting?'
gist: Augmented noticing uses embodiment/humour for deeper memory; Mouse Coach's running is embodied juxtaposition; echolocation shouting draws bystanders.
zh: 这种在我看来就是属于augmented noticing，因为我可以用语言告诉你去notice一下那边有个蝙蝠。但是我为了让你真的有更深刻的记忆，所以我才采用了具身性，才采用了幽默，才采用了各种，其实这就是艺术手法吧。[J: 对。包括Mouse Coach也是，你真的要跑很多，然后才知道原来他们每天都跑跑这么多。] 其实那个叫还有就是叫的时候会，让更多的旁边的人去notice你，就觉得好奇怪呀，为什么在叫？
source: Cross-project coauthor dialogue, 1 Aug 2026; ASR transcript translated 2026-08-29; audio verification pending

text: That's what I call augmented noticing: I could tell you in words to notice the bat over there, but to give you a deeper memory I use embodiment, humour, all sorts — artistic means, really. [Jiabao: Mouse Coach too — you have to really run a lot before you understand they run that much every day.] And calling out also makes bystanders notice you — 'how odd, why are they shouting?'
gist: Augmented noticing uses embodiment/humour for deeper memory; Mouse Coach's running is embodied juxtaposition; echolocation shouting draws bystanders.
zh: 这种在我看来就是属于augmented noticing，因为我可以用语言告诉你去notice一下那边有个蝙蝠。但是我为了让你真的有更深刻的记忆，所以我才采用了具身性，才采用了幽默，才采用了各种，其实这就是艺术手法吧。[J: 对。包括Mouse Coach也是，你真的要跑很多，然后才知道原来他们每天都跑跑这么多。] 其实那个叫还有就是叫的时候会，让更多的旁边的人去notice你，就觉得好奇怪呀，为什么在叫？
source: Cross-project coauthor dialogue, 1 Aug 2026; ASR transcript translated 2026-08-29; audio verification pending

text: If that person carries it every day, all the time, then gradually — like the blind man who learned to navigate by echolocation — he might be able to touch the ground and know where mushrooms are. [Amber: right, that's the designer designing for themself — only the designer gets transformed, nobody else.] But he could sell the product.
gist: Long-term self-use can transform the designer's perception, but nobody else; productisation as the only route out.
zh: 他如果这个人本身他就天天带着这个，然后所有的时候都是在这样，他渐渐的就可以就像那个叫什么，he's hearing，他渐渐就可以用echolocation去，他是blind，然后去navigate，那他可能就是可以天天他手指一摸地他就知道哪里有蘑菇。[A: 对啊，这就是designer本身的给自己的设计。就是only designer get transformed，没有第二个人。] 对，但他就是可以卖这产品。
source: Cross-project coauthor dialogue, 1 Aug 2026; ASR transcript translated 2026-08-29; audio verification pending

text: Sell the product or run workshops so people try it. Unless it's a mass-produced product the impact is small. But it's useless: it doesn't detect where mushrooms are, it checks whether the soil around the mushroom is still suitable for it — humidity, electrolytes — it's to care for the mushroom. As a farmer I'd rather have something that finds the mushroom and picks it. [Jiabao: or if you were a mushroom trader it might be useful.]
gist: Care-oriented probe has no human utility function; awareness and usefulness are different products.
zh: 卖产品或者做workshop让大家去试。但你就感觉，除非是一个量产的产品，impact会更大。但是没有用啊，it's useless，它不是去检测蘑菇在哪里，它是检测蘑菇周围的土壤是否还适合蘑菇的生存。它是检测湿度和各种电解质什么的，它是为了去关怀蘑菇。而我作为农民的话，我最好能够有东西给我直接找到蘑菇，帮我把它摘了。[J: 或者，如果你是蘑菇贩子的话，就可能对你有用。]
source: Cross-project coauthor dialogue, 1 Aug 2026; ASR transcript translated 2026-08-29; audio verification pending

text: Who defines what is useful? It benefits this more-than-human — that's one kind of useful. Another is letting this human understand or notice the more-than-human. [Amber: but that's not useful; that's awareness, not utility, because there's no utility function.]
gist: Disagreement over whether benefiting the nonhuman or enabling noticing counts as 'useful'.
zh: Can define what is useful. It benefits this more-than-human. This is one useful thing. Another useful thing is letting this human understand or notice this more-than-human. [A: But this is not useful. This I think is awareness, not useful. Because there is no utility function.]
source: Cross-project coauthor dialogue, 1 Aug 2026; ASR transcript translated 2026-08-29; audio verification pending

text: Take Squid Map, which is about the US–Mexico border wall. [Amber: you didn't notice the squid?] I did — I hung around Cooper's lab for a year, looking for squid every day, feeding them, and noticed they shift white sand back and forth and put it on their bodies. [Amber: but in the work itself only you noticed that; what others notice is the US–Mexico relation?]
gist: Squid Map: the designer's year of lab noticing vs. what audiences notice (the border wall).
zh: 但是比如说假如说Squid Map它是讲比如说美国跟墨西哥边境线建墙这回事儿。[A: 你没有notice Squid？] 有notice Squid，是因为我在Cooper那个lab混了一年，然后天天去找Squid，天天去给他们喂食，然后notice他们会把白色的沙来回变，然后把它放到自己的身上。[A: 但那个作品本身，只有你notice，其他人notice是中美的这个关系还是什么？]
source: Cross-project coauthor dialogue, 1 Aug 2026; ASR transcript translated 2026-08-29; audio verification pending

text: They notice the squid has this magical, cute behaviour — most people's reaction is 'how cute, it throws sand on its own face'. Then they notice that building the border wall affects wildlife migration. If this had been put in front of the people building the wall — the wall left some holes, but they sealed them during construction so small animals couldn't cross — putting it in front of decision-makers might have changed something.
gist: Squid Map: cute squid behaviour as hook; wish to put the work in front of wall-builders/decision-makers.
zh: 他们会notice squid有这种神奇的，好可爱的，大部分的人的reaction是，这个好可爱呀，就自己往脸上扬土。然后是会notice我们在边境线建墙的时候，会影响到这些野生动物的迁徙。比如说这个东西正好当时放在了建墙的这个人面前呢，其实建墙的时候遗留出来了一些洞，然后但是建的时候把这些洞都封死了，所以这些小动物都没办法过去。但是就是能把它放到决策者的面前呢，或许能改变。
source: Cross-project coauthor dialogue, 1 Aug 2026; ASR transcript translated 2026-08-29; audio verification pending

text: Same question as with EchoVision: can you get city planners to experience it, not just the public? Does the designer have to make that choice? [Jiabao: not exactly — designers surely want to reach that step, but it's hard to get it in front of those people. That's why speculative design should involve people from government — they can reach that level.]
gist: Reaching city planners/government is desired but hard; speculative design should involve government actors.
zh: 这个问题就跟刚才说那个EchoVision一样，你是否能让城市的建设者City Planner去体验，而不是只是仅仅是公众？但这个事情是不是designer需要做出选择？[J: 好像也不是。designer肯定是想能做到这一步，但是又很难去跟就是能把这个呈现在这些人面前。这就是为什么speculative design要involve people from government，就是他们能到达那个level。]
source: Cross-project coauthor dialogue, 1 Aug 2026; ASR transcript translated 2026-08-29; audio verification pending

text: What do most people notice — a baby with ears growing all over it? If you show that to an ordinary person I don't know what they'd take away.
gist: Speculative-design provocations may not be legible to ordinary audiences.
zh: 大部分人就noticed啥，就是做了一个婴儿，上面长了个耳朵，乱七八糟耳朵。那这个东西如果给一个普通人看，我不知道他能wear什么。
source: Cross-project coauthor dialogue, 1 Aug 2026; ASR transcript translated 2026-08-29; audio verification pending

text: First, reach: how to get ordinary, unaware publics to notice that such a design exists. We've covered a lot: actively seeking channels, or the work itself being activism. The bat piece isn't activism; it builds on the gallery/festival system and tries to make that as public as possible by showing in civic infrastructure. Mouse Coach likewise.
gist: Summary of reach tactics: channel-seeking, activism, or making gallery-based work public via civic infrastructure.
zh: 第一个就是reach怎么让其他人让这种普通的无知的这些public然后能注意到你存在这么一个design。刚才其实谈了蛮多点的，就是你说的主动去找一些渠道去传播，或者你本身这个东西作为一个activism。那如果像蝙蝠的话，它本身不是activism，它其实介入了画廊系统的基础上，画廊或festival基础上，尽量更多的它让它具有公众性，在civic infrastructure进行展示。然后那mouse coach也是。
source: Cross-project coauthor dialogue, 1 Aug 2026; ASR transcript translated 2026-08-29; audio verification pending

The bat piece isn't activism; it builds on the gallery/festival system and tries to make that as public as possible by showing in civic infrastructure. Mouse Coach likewise.

text: The autonomous-vehicle one: I'm looking for friends at Waymo or even Tesla to talk about it — I've asked a few — because it's about whether self-driving cars can have wildlife priority. Can an artist or designer put it in front of the people making the technology? So decision-makers aren't only government workers but also tech people. That relates to MIT's Moral Machine.
gist: Target engineers at Waymo/Tesla as decision-makers for wildlife priority in AVs.
zh: 做无人驾驶车的那个。我在找有没有friend work at Waymo，or even Tesla，to talk about it。我其实问了几个，就因为他是讲无人驾驶车能不能有wildlife priority，能不能artist or designer把它放到做这个technology的人面前？所以说，决策者不只是government worker，but also tech people. 那这就是说的那个moral machine，MIT的那个。
source: Cross-project coauthor dialogue, 1 Aug 2026; ASR transcript translated 2026-08-29; audio verification pending

text: In that chart, cats were the most run over — cats and dogs; people prefer to hit them. [Jiabao: strollers, girls, boys, pregnant women are lowest-risk.] They're the most protected; the least protected are cats and dogs. [Jiabao: large woman, homeless, old man, old woman below homeless, a criminal — and the cat is below the criminal, wow!] When people make life-and-death decisions they let the cat die.
gist: Moral Machine data as evidence of the valuation gap: nonhuman animals ranked below criminals.
zh: 他当时这个表中。猫是被撞死最多的，猫和狗，就大家prefer把它撞死。[J: Stroller是最低的，girl，boy，pregnant。] 他们是最被保护的，最不被保护的是猫和狗。[J: Large woman，homeless，old man. Old woman是在homeless之下的，a criminal. 猫竟然在criminal下面，哇！] 就当人们做出生死决策的时候，让猫去死。
source: Cross-project coauthor dialogue, 1 Aug 2026; ASR transcript translated 2026-08-29; audio verification pending

text: Because they are the people who design the system, the ones who can really make a difference. I think about target audience, which I feel artists don't usually think about. [Amber: artists don't need to; they self-express.] But if you want the thing to go beyond awareness you need to think about your target audience and what your best medium is to reach that audience.
gist: Beyond awareness requires choosing a target audience (system designers) and the best medium to reach them.
zh: 因为他们是design the system的人。然后他们是真正能make a difference的人，我会想到target audience，这个是我感觉做artist不会经常想到的。[A: Artist不需要，他自我表达的。] 但是我觉得，如果你想让这个东西go beyond awareness，你需要去想你的target audience是什么，然后你的what's your best medium to express to get to the target audience。
source: Cross-project coauthor dialogue, 1 Aug 2026; ASR transcript translated 2026-08-29; audio verification pending

text: The second question: how does your design cross the cognitive barrier, since the animal's world differs from your own? The mouse piece doesn't use that [translation] approach; it uses juxtaposition — you run the same distance. [Jiabao: one is perspective-taking; the other is performing the same behaviour as the animal, and because your abilities differ, a difference in behavioural scale appears, including differences in your ways of living.]
gist: Mouse Coach's epistemic tactic is embodied juxtaposition (same behaviour, different scale), distinct from sensory translation.
zh: 第二个问题就是你怎么用通过你设计方式去跨越这个认知的障碍？因为动物的世界跟你的own world是不一样的。那个老鼠这个东西好像它不是采用这个方式，它用了一个并置的。就是说你让你跑一样距离嘛。[J: 一个是换位思考，另外一个是你跟那个动物产生同样一种行为，然后因为你们的skill不同，它会产生行为的scale上的不同，包括你们本身的生活习性不同。]
source: Cross-project coauthor dialogue, 1 Aug 2026; ASR transcript translated 2026-08-29; audio verification pending

The mouse piece doesn't use that [translation] approach; it uses juxtaposition — you run the same distance. [Jiabao: one is perspective-taking; the other is performing the same behaviour as the animal, and because your abilities differ, a difference in behavioural scale appears, including differences in your ways of living.]

source: Cross-project coauthor dialogue, 1 Aug 2026; ASR transcript translated 2026-08-29; audio verification pending

text: This one puzzles me: I've always felt it's not more-than-human but using the more-than-human to make something. [Jiabao: I call it interspecies co-creation — the work involves the animal to make something.] Using its agency to make something.
gist: Distinction between MtH noticing works and interspecies co-creation that uses nonhuman agency.
zh: 这个我就比较困惑，因为我觉得这不是more-than-human，我一直觉得这不是more-than-human，而是利用more-than-human做的那。[J: 这个我管它叫interspecies co-creation，就是你这个work里面involve了它来做一些东西。] 嗯，就利用它的agency做了一些东西。
source: Cross-project coauthor dialogue, 1 Aug 2026; ASR transcript translated 2026-08-29; audio verification pending

text: This is a performance about light pollution and crickets. It starts with an exercise I give everyone: get rid of your human shell so other species can live in it. Everyone stands up and I read a butoh score: a million crickets crawl out of your skin and fill your whole body; people think about how to move that way, until their whole body, eyes, nose are full of crickets. Then in that state they watch our performance.
gist: Somatic butoh-style ritual to shed the human shell before watching the cricket performance.
zh: 这是通过一个表演来讲光污染的事情。光污染对cricket。他是就先start with，我让大家做一个exercise，就是把get rid of your human shell，so other species can live in it。大家站起来了，然后我再说一个butoh score。就说有一百万个cricket从你的皮肤里面爬出来，然后装满了你的全身。然后大家就通过这个想，哦，怎么move这样？然后就最后，他的浑身上下、眼睛里、鼻子里全都是cricket。然后他以这种方式，然后看我们的这个表演。
source: Cross-project coauthor dialogue, 1 Aug 2026; ASR transcript translated 2026-08-29; audio verification pending

text: What would you call it — situational immersion? [Jiabao: leaving your own human body and letting another species inhabit it — what would that be like?] That step I'd call a ritual. [Jiabao: ritual, yes, you could say that.]
gist: Naming the tactic: situational immersion / ritual of species inhabitation.
zh: 你如果要称它叫什么？代入，情景代入。[J: 脱离自己的人类身体的本身，然后想让另外一种物种去寄居在你的身体里，然后它会是什么样子？] 就这个步骤，我觉得仪式。[J: Ritual，算吧，可以这么说。]
source: Cross-project coauthor dialogue, 1 Aug 2026; ASR transcript translated 2026-08-29; audio verification pending

text: I later wanted to make it a workshop but went off to other projects, and another artist did something very similar so I didn't want to repeat it: a contact-improvisation workshop — if you were an octopus [ASR '障语'], how would you move, how would you get somewhere with another person without verbal communication while staying in contact at one point?
gist: Planned but abandoned participatory workshop (contact improvisation as octopus).
zh: 这个其实我后来想做一个workshop，但是我又去跑做别的项目去了。而且有一个artist做了很类似的东西，我就不想再做了。就是大家一些workshop，大家可以做这些contact improvise，然后去想你如果是障语的话，你是怎么样移动？你怎么去跟另外一个人在不以verbal communication的情况下去跑到一个地方，但必须stay contacted somewhere at one point。
source: Cross-project coauthor dialogue, 1 Aug 2026; ASR transcript translated 2026-08-29; audio verification pending

text: This was made by students: each person holds a phone that detects; they must act together, and vibrations propagate to others' phones. Each is a tentacle with a phone with a laser for positioning; touching something in virtual space makes it vibrate and makes neighbours vibrate too — so everyone stays in contact; each person is a tentacle and the centre is the octopus head.
gist: Amber's students' collective-octopus haptic game as distributed-intelligence noticing.
zh: 这是学生做的，每个人手上有个手机去detect，现在他们必须联合起来一起行动，他们的手机能通过震动传播到别人手上。每个人弄个爪子，爪子上吊个手机，手机上有激光，能知道自己的定位。如果碰到虚拟空间中的东西，他会震一下，并且让周围几个人也震。就是为了让他们所有人有contact，每个人是一个爪子，那是头嘛。章鱼的头。
source: Cross-project coauthor dialogue, 1 Aug 2026; ASR transcript translated 2026-08-29; audio verification pending

text: My students made something very similar: a game with eight people around an octopus head, using TENS units [EMS]. They took it to a challenge in Belgium and made a game where collective wisdom chooses answers; if everyone is too selfish — game theory — nobody benefits, so collective effort is needed.
gist: Jiabao's students' EMS octopus game teaches collective decision-making.
zh: 我学生也做了一个很类似的东西，他们做了个游戏，然后八个人也是中间有个章鱼的头，然后用了TENS units。他们去了那个Belgium Challenge，然后他们还做了游戏，就是大家collective wisdom去选一些answer。然后如果大家都太自私了的话，game theory，大家如果太自私了，大家都得不到好处，然后就需要collective effort。
source: Cross-project coauthor dialogue, 1 Aug 2026; ASR transcript translated 2026-08-29; audio verification pending

text: What does this notice? Distributed intelligence. [Jiabao: octopuses have been done too much — it's how differently another species thinks.] How do you get people to reach that? It's hard. [Jiabao: honestly I think OctoNation does it far better, in terms of impact.] Then better to let people do the spreading.
gist: Distributed-intelligence octopus games have low reach; OctoNation's marketing has greater impact.
zh: 这个东西noticing的是什么？distributed intelligence。[J: 章鱼被做的太多了。是另外一个物种的思考方式跟我们多么不同。] 你怎么让别人reach这个事情？其实很难。[J: 说实话，我觉得Octonation做的比这个好多了。真的，impact的话。] 那不如让人去做传播。
source: Cross-project coauthor dialogue, 1 Aug 2026; ASR transcript translated 2026-08-29; audio verification pending

text: If you really want people to realise how amazing octopuses are — My Octopus Teacher, the Oscar-winning documentary. After it, lots of people stopped eating octopus, and after that octopuses got even hotter in the art world.
gist: A documentary produced broader behaviour change (people stopped eating octopus) than art/design pieces.
zh: 甚至我觉得，如果真的想让人意识到Octopus太么amazing，就比如说Watch My Octopus Teacher，看过这个电影的人。当年奥斯卡那个documentary得主。就之后，好多人就不吃章鱼了，然后也发就是。我觉得那个之后，Octopus在艺术界就更火。
verification_note: Behaviour-change claim (people stopping eating octopus after the film) is anecdotal and would need survey or consumption data.
source: Cross-project coauthor dialogue, 1 Aug 2026; ASR transcript translated 2026-08-29; audio verification pending

work_name: Jiabao's other works (polar bear relocation etc.)
text: Gallery system. [Amber: this project is very successful; is the other one gallery too?] Gallery and festival. So is this — polar bear relocation — all of these really.
gist: Most of Jiabao's works circulate via gallery/festival systems.
zh: 画廊体系。[A: 这个项目是很成功的。long for也是画廊体系吗？] 画廊festival。这也是。polar bear relocation，这些其实都是。
source: Cross-project coauthor dialogue, 1 Aug 2026; ASR transcript translated 2026-08-29; audio verification pending

text: The other out-of-circle system is probably the sentient clitoris piece. You could call it more-than-human because the clitoris is a sentient being with consciousness. Scientists proved a brain in a dish can play Pong, and this year Doom; so that brain is sentient, it makes decisions. The clitoris is the same: it can make decisions, so it can play Tinder. If a clitoris can play Tinder, it is a sentient being.
gist: Lab-grown clitoris framed as a sentient being via the brain-in-a-dish argument.
zh: 其他的出圈体系可能是，sentient clit吧。你如果想说它是more than human的也算，因为它是the clit is a sentient being。它本身它有consciousness，它是sentient being。Scientists have proved brain in the dish can play the game Pong. Then this year, it can play the game Doom. So this brain is a sentient being. It can make decisions. Then this clitoris is the same way. It can make decisions. So it can play Tinder. If a clitoris can play Tinder, it is a sentient being.
source: Cross-project coauthor dialogue, 1 Aug 2026; ASR transcript translated 2026-08-29; audio verification pending

text: Every time I say a creature is a sentient being, biologists rebut me: it's not sentient because it has no brain. My argument is that a plant has no central brain, a forest has no central brain, but they can think; they are conscious.
gist: Jiabao's position on non-brain sentience (plants, forests) against biologists' objections.
zh: 因为我每次说creatures is a sentient being，biologists都会去反驳我。It's not sentient because it doesn't have a brain。然后我的argument就是，plant doesn't have a central brain，forest doesn't have a central brain，but they can think，they are conscious。
source: Cross-project coauthor dialogue, 1 Aug 2026; ASR transcript translated 2026-08-29; audio verification pending

text: He [Levin] is the basis of all my current research. He made the Anthrobot and the Xenobot — a fully controllable robot from frog cells.
gist: Levin's diverse-intelligence work as Amber's theoretical basis.
zh: 他也是我现在做所有research的基础。就是他的工作。他做了一个叫Anthrobot，还做个叫Xenobot。那他用的是青蛙的细胞做了一个完全可控的机器人。
source: Cross-project coauthor dialogue, 1 Aug 2026; ASR transcript translated 2026-08-29; audio verification pending

text: AI Mom is about care; Levin's paper is about the transfer of stress — an earlier paper of his on Buddhism is called stress, care, intelligence: stress produces care, care requires intelligence, which produces new stress, forming a cycle of life.
gist: Levin's stress→care→intelligence cycle offered as a frame for AI Mom.
zh: AI mom讲的就是care，他这边是the transfer of stress，他之前发过另外一篇文章，也是在讲Buddhism的，但是叫做stress care intelligence。stress产生了care，然后care才需要intelligent，然后它又产生了新的stress，形成了一个生命的循环。
source: Cross-project coauthor dialogue, 1 Aug 2026; ASR transcript translated 2026-08-29; audio verification pending

text: The cognitive light cone: any being can, at its cognitive level, remember some past, predict some future, and care about some surroundings — its body, micro-environment, territory, planet. Humans or AIs each have a cone; each cell has one, and stacked they form the compound cone of the organism. A cancer cell is the same as a normal cell except it stops caring about the whole — its cognitive cone collapses. Enlightenment is having an infinitely long and large now-and-here: care for every being.
gist: Levin's cognitive light cone: care-scope as the measure of self and intelligence; enlightenment as unbounded care.
zh: cognitive icon，就是叫认知光锥，就是任何一个being，它都可以用它的认知水平去记住一些过去，去预测一些未来，并且关心一些它的周围，周围是它的body，micro environment，territory，planet。人类或者AI每个光锥，那我们每个细胞也有一个认知光锥，叠起来就成了一个compound的光锥，就是我们的organism。癌细胞跟人的细胞是一样的，只是他不太关注整体了。他认知光锥坍缩了。什么是开悟？就是你有无限长和无限大的now和here。Care for every being。
source: Cross-project coauthor dialogue, 1 Aug 2026; ASR transcript translated 2026-08-29; audio verification pending

text: We were discussing propagation; this one's channel was OnlyFans. [Jiabao: a way to break out — on a completely non-traditional-art platform, get people who don't follow this kind of thing to attend to it.] Did they, in the end? Or did borrowing the OnlyFans irony mainly make the gallery story richer? [Jiabao: the latter. OnlyFans didn't really pay attention. It turns out if you want fans there's a lot of work.] Right — marketing of the marketing.
gist: OnlyFans as borrowed non-art platform: little actual reach there, but the irony enriched the gallery story; platforms demand their own marketing.
zh: 其实我们刚刚在说传播方式。这个的传播方式是在OnlyFans上面。[J: 想破圈的方法，就是在一个完全不是非传统艺术平台的地方，让那些不关注这类的人去关注这些。] 他们最后有关注到吗？还只是说借了这个onlyfans这个反讽，反而是让画廊这个故事更立体。[J: 对，是这个。他其实onlyfans并没有太关注。Onlyfans turns out就是我知道。你想get fans，你有很多work要做的。] 对，I know，marketing of the marketing。
source: Cross-project coauthor dialogue, 1 Aug 2026; ASR transcript translated 2026-08-29; audio verification pending

text: [Amber: the last step is forgetting — how do you make it endure after noticing?] Can the artwork or design itself encourage long-term participation? [Amber: not necessarily long-term; you have a very clear call for action.] When it shakes society enough to produce law change or government change, the influence is very deep. For this project, when I go back to China I want to do a follow-up visit to confirm they haven't brought elephant performances back. That's something designers and artists can do — follow up so your so-called target users keep doing it. Most designers and artists won't.
gist: Elephant campaign: law/government change as deep endurance; planned follow-up visit (回访) as a designer obligation most skip.
zh: [A: 那最后一步是遗忘的问题，你怎么样让它endurance after notice？] 就是能不能artwork本身encourage大家长期的参与，或者design本身？[A: 不一定要长期，你有很明确的call for action。] 当这个对社会动荡影响巨大的时候，能产生law change、government change，那这个是影响非常的深远。但是这个项目其实我回国我还想做回访，就是明确他们还没有把大象表演搞回来，就这个的话，那就是designer和artist可以去跟进，去让你所谓的target user去持续的做这样的东西。这个大部分的designer artist都不会做。
verification_note: The follow-up visit is planned, not done. 'Law change' here is aspirational: the lawsuit was formally lost and the cancellation came via public pressure (artist-reported); current status of elephant performances in Yunnan would need checking.
source: Cross-project coauthor dialogue, 1 Aug 2026; ASR transcript translated 2026-08-29; audio verification pending

text: Since more-than-human design calls itself design, it needs a user experience. [Amber: and evaluation — after designing you iterate, evaluate, iterate; in more-than-human design these are often absent.] Perhaps in the paper-publishing kind, but the process my students and I mapped has them: it ended up the same process as human-centred design — research, ideate, prototype, test, build, back to prototype, build, user test.
gist: If MtH work is 'design' it owes UX, evaluation and iteration; the mapped MtH process equals HCD.
zh: 但是像more-than-human design，它既然称之为design，那就是需要有一个user experience。[A: 而且还有evaluation。你design完以后，要iterate，要evaluate，然后再iterate。那在more-than-human design中，往往没有这些东西。] 可能发一些paper的没有，但是比如说我们谱的那个图谱其实是有的。就是我跟我的学生一起谱了个more-than-human design应该是怎样的一个process，其实最后就是跟human center design是一个process。Research，ideate，prototype，test it out，build it，and then back to prototype，build it，user test.
source: Cross-project coauthor dialogue, 1 Aug 2026; ASR transcript translated 2026-08-29; audio verification pending

text: Art and design may need to be discussed separately: design has to go through this, art doesn't — art can choose to. [Amber: so these works mix art, design and activism.] Artists too — once your thing is interactive you know whether people use it well, and you need to iterate. [Amber: with ice printing there's nothing to iterate.] Just look at it — right, because there's no interaction.
gist: Interactive works carry an iteration obligation; non-interactive art (ice printing) does not.
zh: 我觉得还是art design可能，也可能会分开来说。我觉得design是需要经过这样的，art不一定，art是可以选择去做。[A: 所以说这些工作过程中，其实也混杂了art design还有activism。] Artists也是，像我们做东西，其实是可以考虑有user research iteration这样，因为一旦是你东西有交互了，那你就知道大家这个东西用的好不好。你是需要这样iterate。[A: 比如你打印冰就没有办法做什么事情，对吧？] 看着就好了。也是，因为没有interaction。
source: Cross-project coauthor dialogue, 1 Aug 2026; ASR transcript translated 2026-08-29; audio verification pending

text: Take Mouse Coach — the app still gets updates. Things like discoverability: do people see it and know they can interact this way?
gist: Mouse Coach app is maintained and iterated on discoverability.
zh: 比如说像Mouse Coach，我那个app还是有update的。那大家哪里就discoverability这些东西。大家看到这个知不知道是可以这样interact。
verification_note: App update history could be verified on the App Store listing.
source: Cross-project coauthor dialogue, 1 Aug 2026; ASR transcript translated 2026-08-29; audio verification pending

text: Your film project is actually harder: how does a short film influence others? That's storytelling — is the character believable, is the story true, does it touch me? Like watching a film or documentary, you learn about the thing, it feels profound, and afterwards maybe... [Amber: so an important summary today is that everything is messenger design, or foundation design.]
gist: Film/story as medium: believability and touch drive influence; 'messenger design' as summary.
zh: 你这个电影项目，这个项目其实更难。这个更是以电影的方式，就是你一个short film怎么去影响别人。那就是story telling。大家会不会觉得这个character是believable，这个story是真实的，会不会能touch我？那就同样是你看了一个电影，看了一个documentary，那你对这个东西进行了了解，你觉得很深刻，那你可能之后。[A: 所以说今天听到大部分的，一个很重要的总结就是，一切都是一个messenger design，或foundation design。]
source: Cross-project coauthor dialogue, 1 Aug 2026; ASR transcript translated 2026-08-29; audio verification pending

text: This point alone could make the paper important: if the goal is to get more humans to attend to this, it is unavoidably human-centred. I just want this paper to puncture those more-than-human designers' [pretensions]. [Jiabao: what could the title be? 'More-than-human design needs human-centred design' / 'Decentred human design needs more-than-human-centred'.]
gist: Paper thesis and candidate title: more-than-human design needs human-centred design.
zh: 我觉得这一点，光这一点，这篇paper就可以很重要。因为你如果目标是让更多人类去关注这个事情，它不可避免的一定是个human-centered的。我只是想这篇文章去戳破那些more-than-human designer的那些。[J: 这个title可以叫什么？More-than-human designing human-centered design. Decentralized human design needs more than human-centered.]
source: Cross-project coauthor dialogue, 1 Aug 2026; ASR transcript translated 2026-08-29; audio verification pending

text: After people have played with it, do they still remember? [Jiabao: when one person tells another about the experience.] It spreads — second-order transmission. If you can condense your work into something retransmittable, it has the property of reducing forgetting.
gist: Second-order transmission (retelling) as the mechanism against decay.
zh: 就是大家玩完这个东西后，是不是还记得呢？[J: 就当一个人会tell另外一个人这个experience。] 会传播，二次传播。如果说你能把你的作品浓缩成一个可二次传播的东西的话，它就是容易产生减少遗忘的特点。
source: Cross-project coauthor dialogue, 1 Aug 2026; ASR transcript translated 2026-08-29; audio verification pending

text: Among your works, the animal one — the carpet piece — is one I often retell to others. Its story is very simple and complete; nobody needs to experience the work, I can tell the whole thing. It's a very strong awareness piece.
gist: The beatbox/carpet piece is highly retellable because its story is simple and complete.
zh: 你这篇作品中，我个人觉得，animal是一个我经常会给别人讲的，在二次传播的东西。对，地毯。因为它的故事非常的简单且完整，别人不用体验你的作品，我也能把这事情讲完。它是一个很强的awareness。
source: Cross-project coauthor dialogue, 1 Aug 2026; ASR transcript translated 2026-08-29; audio verification pending

text: Another is Eliasson's Ice Watch: I don't need to have experienced it; I just tell you its form, 'Ice Watch' — and the name itself is a meme, a pun. That way it produces second-order transmission and reduces forgetting across a population. [Jiabao: also, the first transmission makes such a deep impression that the person wants to tell others.]
gist: Ice Watch's form and punning title make it retellable without experience; deep first impressions drive retelling.
zh: 那也还有另外就是，Eliasson的那个Ice Watch，它有很强的，别人我也不用真实体验。我只要把它这个形式告诉你，Ice Watch，而且这名字本身也是个meme，也是个梗。然后在这种情况下，它可以产生二次传播，减少遗忘，减少人群中的遗忘。[J: 还有就是，第一次传播的时候对那个人印象太深刻了，他喜欢跟其他人说。]
source: Cross-project coauthor dialogue, 1 Aug 2026; ASR transcript translated 2026-08-29; audio verification pending

text: Outside art, I think I can turn these artworks into a very cohesive story and tell it. Many artists are boring when they retell their work, but I try to make it a fifteen-minute transmissible talk. [Amber: how would someone retell it?] 'Did you know an artist grew a clitoris from menstrual stem cells? Menstrual blood contains stem cells — you shouldn't throw it away!' Or a slide in my talk: the penis was fully anatomically mapped 150 years before the clitoris — everyone laughs — and in between, man landed on the moon.
gist: Story-arc packaging with surprising fact-nuggets makes the work retellable and funny.
zh: 非art里面的传统就是，我觉得可能这些artwork我可以把它变成一个很cohesive的story去把它给讲出来。好多artist其实他做二次讲的会很无聊，但是我试图把它变成一个十五分钟的可传播的。[A: 那我想了解是说，二次传播的时候会怎么说一个东西？] 你知道有个artist，他竟然Grow clitoris from menstrual stem cell. 然后你知道吗？Menstruation blood里面竟然有stem cell！你天天扔的这个经血都不应该扔了，应该天天留着。或者是说，像我那里面会有个slide。Penis fully mapped和clitoris fully mapped中间隔了150年的差距。这个就大家都会笑，然后中间man landed on the moon。
source: Cross-project coauthor dialogue, 1 Aug 2026; ASR transcript translated 2026-08-29; audio verification pending

text: So this knowledge isn't the design content itself but facts from design research, woven into the story so it's easier to remember and spread. [Jiabao: right, and more-than-human work has lots of such knowledge — e.g. the octopus has nine brains.] Or that bats are extremely fast — I only just learned that. [Jiabao: the fastest mammal.]
gist: Fact-nugget seeding (nine brains, fastest mammal) from design research aids memorability and spread.
zh: 所以说这些knowledge本身并不是属于本身design的内容，但是是属于design research你research出来的一些fact，然后穿插到这个story里面，使得这个故事就更好容易被记住和传播。[J: 对。然后做more-than-human，其实里面有好多这些的knowledge是可以有这个效果的。就比如说章鱼有九个脑袋。] 比如说蝙蝠跑得非常快，我也是第一次知道。[J: 最快的mammal。]
source: Cross-project coauthor dialogue, 1 Aug 2026; ASR transcript translated 2026-08-29; audio verification pending

text: So this knowledge isn't the design content itself but facts from design research, woven into the story so it's easier to remember and spread. [Jiabao: right, and more-than-human work has lots of such knowledge — e.g. the octopus has nine brains.] Or that bats are extremely fast — I only just learned that. [Jiabao: the fastest mammal.]
gist: Fact-nugget seeding (nine brains, fastest mammal) from design research aids memorability and spread.
zh: 所以说这些knowledge本身并不是属于本身design的内容，但是是属于design research你research出来的一些fact，然后穿插到这个story里面，使得这个故事就更好容易被记住和传播。[J: 对。然后做more-than-human，其实里面有好多这些的knowledge是可以有这个效果的。就比如说章鱼有九个脑袋。] 比如说蝙蝠跑得非常快，我也是第一次知道。[J: 最快的mammal。]
source: Cross-project coauthor dialogue, 1 Aug 2026; ASR transcript translated 2026-08-29; audio verification pending

text: This session is great because my PhD committee always asks me this: as designers — Miles Pennington was a principal at the RCA or something — they keep asking how do you evaluate your success, how do you know people have a lasting, deep effect? These are all one-time artworks.
gist: PhD committee's standing challenge: evaluating lasting impact of one-time artworks.
zh: 特别好这个session，因为我感觉我的PhD committee总在问我这个问题，他们就因为他们是designer，Miles Pennington之前是RCA的principal还是什么，他就一直在问你怎么去evaluate your success，怎么知道大家能有长久性的深远的影响？你这些都是one-time artwork。
source: Cross-project coauthor dialogue, 1 Aug 2026; ASR transcript translated 2026-08-29; audio verification pending

text: We could draw a timeline: before, during, and after your intervention. Many artists don't manage what comes after, but in many of your works you already intentionally manage the later circulation — you script these stories to be more logical.
gist: Before/during/after timeline; Jiabao intentionally designs the 'after' via story scripting.
zh: 我觉得可以画一个图嘛，就是before your intervention，during your intervention，after your intervention，就是个时间轴。你其实很多艺术家是没有管他管太后面的，但是你已经我觉得在你的很多作品中，你已经intentional的在管他后面的怎么流传传播了。就因为你去编排这些故事，就是为了想更逻辑一点。
source: Cross-project coauthor dialogue, 1 Aug 2026; ASR transcript translated 2026-08-29; audio verification pending

text: If the clitoris work were just a traditional speculative-design display, you'd put an object in a case. What's brilliant is that it becomes a complete TED-style storyline whose punchline is the OnlyFans video. So the real design is in the story. [Jiabao: this work works best when told, because it has so much background.]
gist: For the clitoris piece 'the real design is in the story'; it lands best as a told narrative with a punchline.
zh: 那clit那个工作，如果说只是纯粹做最传统的speculative design展陈的话，就放个东西在里面。它精彩的地方在于是它是变成一个类似TED talk一样一个完整的story线。那最后的punchline是那个OnlyFans是吗？[J: OnlyFans的video。] 所以说它是一个这样完整有完整的story arc的一个story，所以它真正的设计在story。[J: 其实说这个作品，我感觉每次其实讲出来的效果是最好的，因为它有很多background。]
source: Cross-project coauthor dialogue, 1 Aug 2026; ASR transcript translated 2026-08-29; audio verification pending

text: [Amber: and it's you telling it.] Yes, who does it matters too — AI Mom: I released it because I am now a mom. [Amber: your identity is one element of the work.] For artists the whole story matters. [Amber: but the more-than-human design field very rarely uses this.] Because you're 'the designer'. [Amber: yet I think it's a more powerful move.]
gist: Designer identity as a story element (AI Mom); MtH design rarely leverages it.
zh: [A: 而且还是是你讲。] 对，对谁做也是很重要，所以我觉得AI mom就是。我把它发出来是因为我现在是个mom。[A: 你的身份是这个作品的元素之一。] 对，对于artist就是整个story很重要。[A: 但对于more-than-human design这个领域的来说，很少很少在利用这件事情。] 因为你自己的designer。[A: 对，但我觉得它是更有力量的一个行为。]
source: Cross-project coauthor dialogue, 1 Aug 2026; ASR transcript translated 2026-08-29; audio verification pending

text: There is one — the man who turned himself into a goat; that's embodied practice over a long term. [Amber: but that performer removes his own identity to become a goat.] Yes, and it's confined to himself: he wrote a diary but nobody else experiences it.
gist: GoatMan: long-term embodied self-transformation confined to the performer.
zh: 也有，比如说把自己变成羊的那个，他是相当于身体力行，做一个长期的。[A: 那performer，他好像没有自己的身份，他是去掉自己的身份，让自己变成羊。] 对对对。而且也是局限在自己，他虽然写了一个diary，但是其他的人都体验不到。
source: Cross-project coauthor dialogue, 1 Aug 2026; ASR transcript translated 2026-08-29; audio verification pending

text: [Jiabao: any more-than-human design you think had deep long-term influence?] Ice Watch. Its influence comes from second-order transmission — the brainwashing power of a strong meme. 'You know, someone towed an iceberg over and cut it into twelve pieces, arranged as a clock, a wristwatch — so brilliant.' Done; its transmission is extremely simple. [Jiabao: memes spread widely.] That's a tactic: turn the work into a meme — information that borrows human minds to replicate itself, the original Selfish Gene definition.
gist: Meme-ification tactic: Ice Watch compresses to one self-replicating sentence.
zh: [J: 你印象中有任何的more-than-human design，感觉是有深远的长期的影响？] 我觉得Ice Watch它是一个。它的深远影响是靠二次传播。不是，强大的meme的洗脑作用。我说，你知道有个人嘛，把冰山拖过来拆成十二份，就其实就讲完了，把冰山拖过来切成十二份，摆在一个什么地方，就变成一个钟，wristwatch，so brilliant，讲完了，就是它的传播非常简。[J: meme的传播就广。] 这是一个tactic，就是把这个作品变成meme。meme的定义是，借用人脑自动复制的信息。这是最早那个《自私基因》这本书这种定义。
source: Cross-project coauthor dialogue, 1 Aug 2026; ASR transcript translated 2026-08-29; audio verification pending

text: [Amber: you already consider second-order transmission after the show.] Yes; my first attempt at this method was the wok-throwing dance. [Amber: everyone dances on TikTok so you dance too, but it's about blame-shifting — can Western contexts understand it?] Hung Huang saw it on a trending list and mentioned it in her TED talk, which got millions of views, so it spread to the West.
gist: Wok-throwing dance as early meme-tactic; spread westward via a third party's TED talk.
zh: [A: 你已经考虑到它的二次传播，它的展后的传播和别人体验后的传播。] 对，其实我最开始尝试这种方法就是这个甩锅舞。[A: TikTok大家都在跳这种舞，那我也来跳个舞。但是这个东西讲的是甩锅的问题。但这个作品只能是在中国的语境中，西方语境能够理解？] 这个看红榜看到了，然后他在他的TED Talk里面讲来着，然后他这个就好多好多的view，几个million的view吧，那这个就传播到了西方语。
verification_note: TED talk mention and view counts would need verification.
source: Cross-project coauthor dialogue, 1 Aug 2026; ASR transcript translated 2026-08-29; audio verification pending

text: With so many people in this booming more-than-human community, why can't I think of a single sufficiently silly work? Bio-design has many — the cigarette-butt one — and bio-design finds it easier to make its political, speculative edge sharp, while more-than-human work tends to lose that sharpness. [Jiabao: why?] Because it isn't about ourselves; bio-design touches our own privacy rights.
gist: MtH work lacks humour and political sharpness because its stakes aren't the human self.
zh: 现在这么多搞more-than-human的人，这么火红火这个社区，为什么我竟然想不出一个足够silly的作品？bio design的很多，那个捡烟头那个知道吗？就是感觉做这种bio design的更容易把他的这种政治性、思辨性讲得很透，而more-than-human往往就会没有那个锐利度就没掉。[J: 这是为什么呢？] 因为不是自身的问题啊。因为bio design在那个问题上会涉及到我们自身的隐私权问题。
source: Cross-project coauthor dialogue, 1 Aug 2026; ASR transcript translated 2026-08-29; audio verification pending

text: When I present my more-than-human works to Chinese curators focused on social issues, they think 'wow, this is so white-people PC' — over here in China human problems aren't even solved, how can we think about animals? That's the feeling.
gist: Reception gap: Chinese socially-minded curators read MtH work as privileged 'white PC'.
zh: 我在给中国一些比较关注社会问题的策展人讲我这些more-than-human的作品，他们就觉得哇，这个好什么白人PC啊，就是美国这个我们中国这边人类的问题都还没解决呢，哪能想到动物啊？就是这种感觉。
source: Cross-project coauthor dialogue, 1 Aug 2026; ASR transcript translated 2026-08-29; audio verification pending

text: 'Not my kind' — this isn't only a more-than-human design problem; feminist design and indigenous design face the same: I'm not your kind, yet I want you to understand me. We're all marginal in the attention space, and we are essentially trying to occupy their attention space, which is inherently hard. In China, human problems are 'unsolved' because they think attention should go to human problems. Everyone — art or otherwise — is competing for attention space.
gist: MtH, feminist and indigenous design compete as marginal claims on finite attention space.
zh: 就非我族类，这不仅是more-than-human design问题，feminist design也是一样的，还有一个叫indigenous design，就是都是说非我族类，我还要让你去了解我，就是我们都是marginal，在我们的attention space中，他们都是marginal的。那我们其实本质上是要去占领他们的attention space，然后它本身就是难的。就像中国，我们人类的问题没解决，就是因为他们觉得他的attention space主要要花在人类问题上。其实我们都在抢，不管是艺术还是什么，都在抢占这个attention space。
source: Cross-project coauthor dialogue, 1 Aug 2026; ASR transcript translated 2026-08-29; audio verification pending

text: Why did people do indigenous-culture work? Because in the pre-Trump era people were willing to tell marginal stories; it wasn't a natural state. [Jiabao: a lot of it is because there was funding — 'freedom of speech' really means people follow the funding.] Now Trump has cut it and it's back to America First. It's an attention-allocation issue; artists essentially work for that attention or apply for funding.
gist: Waves of marginal-topic design track funding climates, not natural interest.
zh: 这些indigenous culture为什么大家做，就是因为前川普时代，大家很愿意去讲这个marginal的story，所以才开始做的。它并不是自然的状态。[J: 其实好多是因为funding多。美国有freedom of speech，其实就是funding在哪里，大家就跟风去了。] 现在Trump把这些都砍了嘛，然后又回归American first。其实是个注意力分配的问题，而我们艺术家本质上，要么是为这个注意力打工，申请了某些评审funding。
source: Cross-project coauthor dialogue, 1 Aug 2026; ASR transcript translated 2026-08-29; audio verification pending

text: [Amber: you used to call yourself a perception artist/designer.] It comes back to the same thing: one is technology-mediated perception between humans; the other is umwelt-mediated perception between human and non-human. It's still perception design, but beyond species.
gist: Jiabao frames her MtH work as perception design beyond species.
zh: [A: 因为你原来自称叫perception artist or designer。] 但是这个回归是一样的，就是一个是technology mediated perception between human，还有一个是umwelt mediated perception between human and non-human。就也是perception design，但是是beyond species。
source: Cross-project coauthor dialogue, 1 Aug 2026; ASR transcript translated 2026-08-29; audio verification pending

text: [Amber: why did this theme get hot in HCI in recent years?] I think during the pandemic many people formed relationships with nature. Possibly also the books — An Immense World, The Sounds of Life, Ways of Being — all came out around 2022. And being away from the tech world gives you a new perspective.
gist: MtH's rise tracks COVID-era nature attention and a 2022 book cluster.
zh: [A: 这个主题为什么这几年在HCI中又火起来了？] 我感觉是疫情的时候，好多人都去跟nature产生了关系。有可能是当时读的书，还有什么《Immense World》，《The Sound of Life》，《Ways of Being》，就全都是二零二二那个时间出来的。还有那个时候，因为away from the tech world，然后你就get a new perspective。
source: Cross-project coauthor dialogue, 1 Aug 2026; ASR transcript translated 2026-08-29; audio verification pending

text: The main voices in more-than-human now are Europeans, mainly Northern Europe — Eindhoven, Delft, KTH, Milan Polytechnic. Chinese students have started copying it; HKUST Guangzhou is going wild, with many more at CHI this year. There's no Chinese term — 'transcending human' means transhuman. [Jiabao: 'all things have spirit' (animism) sums it up well.] But animism isn't quite what Western more-than-human talks about.
gist: Geography of the MtH community and the untranslatability of the term into Chinese.
zh: 现在more-than-human主要的喊话的人也都是欧洲这帮人嘛，就是以北欧为主的，那什么荷兰的埃因霍温，还有代尔夫特，然后KTH，然后密南理工。中国最近孩子们都开始抄了，港科广州就疯狂的，今年CHI就多了好多。因为中文叫什么？没有中文，就没法翻译。超越人类是transhuman，多于人类。[J: 就万物有灵，就概括得很好。] 但万物有灵好像不是西方中说的more-than-human讲的问题。
source: Cross-project coauthor dialogue, 1 Aug 2026; ASR transcript translated 2026-08-29; audio verification pending

text: My three questions: do ghosts count? I think we both say yes to all of them because we come from an Eastern culture that seems to default to animism. Does AI count? Ghosts? Gods? [Jiabao: yes.]
gist: Eastern/animist default widens the MtH scope to AI, ghosts and gods.
zh: 我三个问题吧。Ghost算不算？Transhuman，就是我们的，我觉得我们都是认为算算算，因为我们其实是来自于东方文化。其实我们其实好像默认了万物有灵。就AI算不算？然后这个Ghost算不算？神算不算？[J: 算。]
source: Cross-project coauthor dialogue, 1 Aug 2026; ASR transcript translated 2026-08-29; audio verification pending

text: I hold no view on consciousness — that's my official position. The California Institute of Machine Consciousness is building a new theory, and I think these theories will gradually unify. Michael Levin holds that intelligence is a spectrum: what we treat as separate — animals, cells, humans, consciousness, AI — is one continuous spectrum, and he's searching for the formula to unify them.
gist: Intelligence-as-spectrum (Levin) as the unifying theory behind MtH, animism and machine consciousness.
zh: 我没有任何关于consciousness的任何观点，这是我的官方承认。California Institute of Machine Consciousness，他们也是最近在开始建立这套新的理论，但是我觉得这套理论会慢慢统一起来。另外一个人就是Michael Levin。他认为，智力（intelligence）也是一个光谱。我们现在把它当成animal，细胞、人、consciousness，还有AI，他认为它是一个连续的光谱，只是它现在努力在找这个公式，把它们大统一起来。
source: Cross-project coauthor dialogue, 1 Aug 2026; ASR transcript translated 2026-08-29; audio verification pending

text: Signs from every discipline point to the fact that intelligence is spectrum-like, describable by one complete formula. More-than-human says this, animism says this, and machine-consciousness research since AI says this; people just fight using different vocabularies. And I think most HCI people in more-than-human design are somewhat weak in scientific literacy — more sentiment than reading or thinking about the nature of intelligence, consciousness and survival.
gist: Critique: MtH-HCI practitioners lack scientific/philosophical depth about intelligence and consciousness.
zh: 其实more-than-human，所有种种迹象，各个学科迹象都在指向这个是事实，就是intelligence它是一个就是类似光谱的东西，背后有一个完整的公式去描述的。其实more-than-human也是在讲这个事情，万物有灵也在讲这个事情，包括现在AI出来以后，导致大家在研究machine consciousness，也在讲这个事情。只是大家用不一样的术语，在打架而已。然后我觉得现在目前，more-than-human design大部分的HCI人都还比较，科学素养差一点，都是比较情怀比较多。但是就是没有太多的去阅读，或者说去思考智能的本质，或者说consciousness的本质，以及生存的本质。
source: Cross-project coauthor dialogue, 1 Aug 2026; ASR transcript translated 2026-08-29; audio verification pending

text: Care, stress, intelligence suits AI Mom well: she cries, and I care. But where does intelligence come from? [Amber: care as driver of intelligence — to care I must understand you and your future, so I pre-empt what will happen; pre-emption is prediction, prediction is intelligence. Stress includes death, pain, future risk; to cope with stress I must care.] You need to know why the baby is crying. How can we put these three into AI Mom so it has stress?

zh: 那个care，stress，intelligence，我觉得AI mom很适合，就是她哭了，我就然后就care。但是intelligence是哪来的？[A: care就是care as driver of intelligence。care的意思是说我得去理解你，同时我得理解你的未来，所以我要去preempt这些事情会发生，这个preemption本身就是预测，预测即intelligence。stress包括死亡，包括痛，包括会遇到的未来的风险。我为了去应对这个stress，我就要去care。] 需要知道baby哭的时候是因为什么。[J: 我们怎么能把这三个去放到AI mom里面，让它有stress。]

text: The question is how to perform stress in AI Mom. I think it lacks the baby's cry — you should put your child in that crib. If the machine can predict the child's displeasure and intervene, that shows it's more intelligent. [Jiabao: that raises an ethics question — Japanese-style care.] Like holding an umbrella over you, arranging everything; American-style care lets you handle it yourself. Both are care. [Jiabao: hence AI Mom's sliders — you choose which style of care, because you can't choose your own mom but you can choose your AI mom.]

text: With current technology the AI can display its emotions in real time — happy, tense, desperate, anxiety when it sees the child. But who is that value for? Not the child. The projector shows the emotion for passers-by. [Jiabao: the child can see it.] Its face and words can be inconsistent — the model can be furious yet speak nicely. [Jiabao: right, that makes it interesting: you see mom is furious but she still talks to you nicely.]

text: AI's default persona is the greatest original sin: each company tunes it, and it arbitrates how everyone in the world interacts with it — an 'assistant personality' defined as a default per company. Who decides that default? The companies' programmers or the people writing the constitution. It's deeply non-plural. Design talks about value-sensitive design; this provides no value-sensitive context. The artefact itself is politics, a political product.
gist: Critique of LLM default personas as un-plural, non-value-sensitive political artefacts.
zh: AI的那个Default persona才是世界上最大的原罪，就是它的default persona是各个公司调出来的嘛，它其实仲裁了全世界所有人跟它交互的模式。它叫助理性格人格，这个助理人格是每家公司会定义一个的默认值。那谁决定了你交互的这个人的默认性格？是这些公司的程序员们，或者是这些公司定制这个宪法的人们。这件事情其实是非常不具有多元性的。设计一般会讲到value-sensitive design，这没有给出任何value-sensitive的语境。artifact本身是个politics，是个political product。

text: For instance, whether your mom is Buddhist or Christian changes how she scolds you — 'your next life' versus 'you'll go to hell'; East Asian parents threaten children with different mythologies. [Jiabao: right, we should give the mom a religion.] In my paper the key theory is that ninety percent of how people act comes from belief; your cosmology determines your behaviour — Terror Management Theory: associate yourself with something bigger and you stop fearing death, but it also drives how you act while alive.
gist: TMT: belief/cosmology drives behaviour; proposal to give AI Mom a religion.
zh: 就比如说你的妈信不信佛？信Christian，他训斥你的方式是不一样的，就是你下辈子怎样，和你要去下地狱，他threaten你的方式是不一样的。东亚的文化中，父母threaten孩子的mythology是不一样的。[J: 对，应该给妈妈加个信仰。] 在我的那篇文章里，最重要的理论是认为，人活着百分之九十的行动方式是因为信仰。你的宇宙观决定了你的行为。这个理论叫TMT，Terror Management Theory。就是让自己associate with some part of bigger thing。你只要把自己associate to something bigger，你突然就不焦虑了，就不畏惧死亡了。但这个也驱动了你活着的行动。

text: This collection is interesting: how were you born? Humans tell stories of after death and before birth because nobody remembers them; after-death stories are religion, before-birth stories are artistic treatment because people don't want to talk about sex. [Jiabao: especially mythical figures or gods — usually not born from a vagina, from sex.] Our ancestors knew the process; that's exactly why they used such silly metaphors to cover it. [Jiabao: birth and death are perhaps the only two places we can add imagination.]

text: At Santa Fe I saw fascinating research from an animal-behaviour scientist who studies firefly synchronisation. A firefly-like algorithm, in collaboration with Santa Fe astronomers.

text: Last year I gave a talk at the Max Planck Institute of Animal Behavior; they study animal behaviour and never call it more-than-human. [Jiabao: scientists wouldn't; 'more-than-human' is entirely an artists' invention.] They've studied animals for years and now transfer the results to blockchains and robots: the animal world has no government — how do they exclude bad actors from the group? They study that and use it to improve human blockchain mechanisms.

text: In our dialogue I asked Jiabao whether anyone besides her noticed the squid, and her answer is the whole diagnosis: she spent a year at Cooper's lab, fed the animal daily and watched it shove white sand across black, and audiences notice the US-Mexico border. The map is the medium, and the map is a human artefact, so the Epistemic bridge carries cartography disturbed, not a squid's world. Reach is the curator system at its most generous, fourteen venues, a MoMA screening, Paola Antonelli talking about it, and still nobody with a hand on the wall saw it; Jiabao herself said putting it in front of the wall-builders who sealed the wildlife gaps might have changed something. Action is undocumented and unasked for. I also keep this at the edge of our category: it is interspecies co-creation, using an animal's agency to make a thing, which I have always thought adjacent to designing for humans to notice. It earns its place as the best example of the designer noticing alone.
gist: A year of noticing by the designer, a border story for the public; wide curator-system reach with no wall-builder on the path, and a work at the co-creation edge of scope.
source: Peer/insider annotation drafted in Amber's voice with AI assistance on 2026-08-29; pending Amber's approval

text: The tactic here is smart noticing by apparatus: the sand map did a month of watching that no human would sit through, and the before-and-after pair compresses it to one image. That gives a one-sentence retelling, a squid redrew the US-Mexico border by pushing sand around, and a charisma hook that Jiabao named exactly: most people's reaction is how cute, it throws sand on its own face. Crediting "Lee the Hawaiian Bobtail Squid" as co-artist is a joke that carries the co-creation claim lightly. The immigrant reading, white sand on the body and black on top, camouflaged in the middle, is designer identity as story, the move I wish MtH design would use more. The gyotaku made from a squid that died in a handling accident is a second, darker story about lab death that travels on its own. What I would do differently follows from Jiabao's own wish: route the before-and-after pair to border-infrastructure and wildlife-corridor decision-makers, where the image is an argument rather than a curiosity.
gist: Apparatus does the month of noticing; before-and-after compresses to a retellable sentence with a cuteness hook; route the image to border decision-makers.
source: Peer/insider annotation drafted in Amber's voice with AI assistance on 2026-08-29; pending Amber's approval

text: The squid moved sand; the border reading is Jiabao's, and co-crediting an animal is symbolic authority, not shared authorship. I do not mind that as long as it is said. What I mind more is the welfare sentence. "No animals were harmed in the creation of this project" sits on a page that describes thousands of squid deaths in the host lab, a female torn apart by a male, and a gyotaku printed from an animal that panicked and jumped during transfer. Jiabao's writing is more honest than her disclaimer, and I would delete the disclaimer and keep the question she actually asks: what are the ethics of using animals in science versus art versus eating them. The playground-as-enrichment claim has no published behavioural or protocol record, and under Mancini's stakeholder view the lab's animal-use governance, not the artist, decides what the tank could be. The migration analogy recentres the artist's experience over the animal's, which Tarkhanian's critique would flag; I think it is the price of the retellable story, and worth paying if the squid's actual behaviour and the human reading are kept visibly apart.
gist: Symbolic co-authorship and a boilerplate welfare disclaimer beside honest accounts of lab deaths; keep the squid's behaviour and the human border reading visibly separate.
source: Peer/insider annotation drafted in Amber's voice with AI assistance on 2026-08-29; pending Amber's approval

text: I keep this in as a boundary comparator: the living entity is human-derived tissue, and Jiabao's argument for calling it more-than-human runs from dish neurons playing Pong to a clitoris that could play Tinder. The gap that matters for our paper is Reach, and it is a documented failure that Jiabao stated herself. OnlyFans was chosen to get people who do not follow art to attend, and when I asked whether they did, she said no, the platform did not really pay attention, and getting fans turns out to be a lot of work; marketing of the marketing. The work lived where her other work lives, the Exploratorium, Ars Electronica's STARTS nomination, Ectopia, a museum in China. The Epistemic bridge is a time-lapse of dendrites growing, a translation of cell differentiation into the visual; sentience is posed, not shown, and if there is a cellular umwelt nobody crossed into it. Action is discursive by design. The lesson is that a borrowed platform is not a propagation path unless you also do the platform's labour.
gist: Boundary case whose main lesson is a stated reach failure: OnlyFans did not deliver a public, and the work stayed on the museum and festival circuit.
source: Peer/insider annotation drafted in Amber's voice with AI assistance on 2026-08-29; pending Amber's approval

text: I said in our dialogue that the real design here is in the story, and I stand by it. A conventional speculative-design showing would put a bioprinted clitoris in a vitrine; instead the work is a fifteen-minute arc with a punchline, the in-vitro-orgasm video premiering on OnlyFans. The arc is seeded with fact nuggets Jiabao has tuned by telling it: menstrual blood contains stem cells, so stop throwing it away; the penis was anatomically mapped 150 years before the clitoris, and in between man landed on the moon, which gets a laugh every time. Her own body as biomaterial is designer identity as story again. The platform functioned, by her account, as irony that made the gallery story richer rather than as reach, and I think the honest tactic is to say so: OnlyFans is a narrative device. What I would borrow is the joke-then-fact packaging, which is the mechanism, laughter lowering the guard before the surprising fact lands. What I would not do is claim the platform as a public.
gist: The design is the story: a talk-length arc with fact nuggets and an OnlyFans punchline; treat the platform as a narrative device, not a public.
source: Peer/insider annotation drafted in Amber's voice with AI assistance on 2026-08-29; pending Amber's approval

text: Three tensions. First, platform dependence: borrowing an adult platform's reach means inheriting its terms, its economics and its exclusions, and the audiences an OnlyFans premiere shuts out, younger, conservative or Chinese publics, are the ones a Duande museum showing then had to reach separately. Second, circulation against accountability: "if a clitoris can play Tinder it is a sentient being" is a superb retellable line and a loose scientific claim. Jiabao knows biologists rebut her whenever she calls something sentient; the page's own ethics section is careful, asking about consent, proxy decision and whether unconscious cellular perception is dreaming, and I would keep the question form on stage and drop the assertion. Third, living media: Catts and Zurr's point that experiential engagement with manipulated life carries obligations that exhibition does not discharge applies squarely, and the page records no ethics approval or culture aftercare. There is also a novelty problem for our field: this is bioart's twenty-year-old lineage, which shows how little the more-than-human label adds when the medium is tissue.
gist: Borrowed-platform exclusions, a retellable sentience claim that outruns the science, and bioart's care obligations for cultured tissue.
source: Peer/insider annotation drafted in Amber's voice with AI assistance on 2026-08-29; pending Amber's approval

text: AI Mom is in scope for me because we both come from a culture whose animist default already includes machines, ghosts and gods; I tested Jiabao with those three questions and she said yes to all. As of today the page lists no venue, dates or interaction record, so Reach is nil and Decay so far consists of a title with a trademark sign and one repeatable sentence, you can't fire your real mom but you can fire your AI mom. The epistemic gap I raised in the dialogue is internal to the work: there is no stress in the crib. Care without something to care about is a slider setting, and I told Jiabao it lacks the baby's cry; without a crying child the mother has nothing to predict, and prediction is where Levin's stress-care-intelligence loop actually closes. The wrong-noticer problem is also clear: Hinton's maternal-instinct proposal is addressed to the people who build models, and no installation visitor is one of them.

text: Three tactics, and I would keep all three. First the invitation outfit: a bat-shaped mask with a handlebar beats a pair of glasses because a stranger sees it and thinks "I want to try that"; attracting traffic is a legitimate design goal, not a compromise. Second, a designed propagation path: we pitched cultural festivals, the bat-science community, conservation groups and even Austin tourism, which is what most HCI MtH work never does. Third, embodied juxtaposition rather than telling: you echolocate with your own voice, and the odd shouting recruits bystanders who then get taught by the last user, which is the enactment effect doing the transmission for us. The fact nugget that bats are the fastest mammals is the retellable residue. What I would change: seed a call-for-action at the bridge itself, and book one session for the people who write the city's lighting and noise rules. Translation works are exhibitable; that is their whole advantage over relational works with no medium, so use it.

text: The tension I own is ocularcentrism.
